description: Verify that a DUT-emitted ARP Reply carrying a Link-Local sender IP is sent via link-layer broadcast (RFC 3927 §2.5, MUST)
approach:
[Objective]
Normal ARP Replies are unicast to the requester, but RFC 3927 §2.5 last MUST flips that for Link-Local: a Reply whose sender_proto_ip is in 169.254/16 must be sent as Ethernet broadcast. This lets every host on the segment refresh its cache so all stale mappings are corrected — important because LL ownership can shift between hosts. This case has the same shape as ADDRESS_SELECTION_16 but adds the broadcast Eth dst check.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: OpStartLLAutoconf (kicks the Link-Local state machine; fast envelope)

2. DUT: 3 Probes → 1st Announce → post_claim entry observer fires:
   • UT-query DUT_LL → snapshot into Captured
   • Tester → DUT: ARP Request, target_proto_ip = DUT_LL (delivered via AIFACE-LL)

3. Observation:
   • DUT → wire: ARP Reply
     - sender_proto_ip = DUT_LL
     - target_proto_ip = AIFACE-LL sender
     - Ethernet dst = FF:FF:FF:FF:FF:FF (broadcast)   ← key check vs _16

[Pass condition]
Claim observed AND DUT-emitted Reply has correct fields AND Ethernet dst = broadcast.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_no_claim_observed — DUT did not announce its committed LL
• Fail_no_responder_reply — DUT did not emit an ARP Reply for the claim address
• Fail_reply_wrong_fields — Reply carried wrong fields or unicast Ethernet destination

verdicts.Pass: DUT-emitted Link-Local Reply is broadcast — normal
verdicts.Fail_no_claim_observed: DUT did not announce its committed Link-Local address
verdicts.Fail_no_responder_reply: DUT did not emit an ARP Reply for the claim address
verdicts.Fail_reply_wrong_fields: DUT's ARP Reply carried wrong fields or unicast Ethernet destination
